goal: Build and read the three classic multi-container Pod patterns — sidecar, adapter and ambassador — plus a v1.29+ native sidecar, and prove what containers in a Pod really share: one network namespace and named volumes, nothing else.
produces: Four running Pods (sidecar, adapter, ambassador, native sidecar) that all consume data/access-seed.log and data/tariff-quote.json
Prometheus-format metrics produced by an adapter container from a proprietary key=value log it did not write
An admission-time validation error proving that each container has its own independent volumeMounts list
concepts: Containers in a Pod share the network namespace and volumes, not the filesystem root or PID namespace
Sidecar adds a capability, adapter reshapes an output, ambassador owns the outbound connection
kubectl logs -c <container> and the error you get when you forget it
Native sidecars: initContainers with restartPolicy: Always (v1.29+, GA v1.33) give ordering guarantees
